issues.description: The valueToMetricFullKey builder duplicates detailedMetric logic with three near-identical branches; the invariant 'when valueToMetric is true, append key_value; otherwise append key' is never stated and is implemented three times.
issues.detail: The three branches (matchedViaWildcard, matchedUsingValue, default-key) all reduce to: if valueToMetric or matchedUsingValue then write key+_+value, else write key. This invariant should be stated in one comment and implemented once. The current decomposition reads as faith-based — the reader cannot verify by inspection that the three paths agree.

issues.description: Dead allocation: NewRateLimit is called and its returned stats immediately overwritten on the next line.
issues.detail: Lines ~425-427 construct a fresh RateLimit via NewRateLimit (which calls statsManager.NewStats(rateLimit.FullKey)) and then immediately replace rateLimit.Stats with NewStats(enhancedKey). The first NewStats call registers an unused stats struct — wasted allocation and a stray metric registration per GetLimit call when keys differ. Either drop the NewRateLimit call or use the enhancedKey directly.

issues.description: GetLimit now allocates a strings.Builder and writes to it on every call, even when no descriptor uses value_to_metric — premature work on the hot path with no measurement.
issues.detail: GetLimit is the per-request hot path. The new valueToMetricFullKey builder runs unconditionally for every request, allocating and appending strings even when the entire config has no value_to_metric flag set. A simple guard (skip the builder unless some ancestor descriptor has valueToMetric) would eliminate the cost for all existing deployments. No benchmark is provided.

issues.description: FullKey is read before being written in the non-detailed branch — relies on an unstated assumption that prior code paths populated rateLimit.FullKey.
issues.detail: The check 'if enhancedKey != rateLimit.FullKey' depends on rateLimit.FullKey being set somewhere upstream. In the detailed-metric branch FullKey is now assigned, but in the non-detailed default path the value of FullKey is the one set at descriptor-load time. This cross-function invariant is load-bearing and undocumented; a future refactor of NewRateLimit could silently break the comparison.

issues.description: The 'No next descriptor found; still append something deterministic' branch is reachable but its output is then discarded — the comment misleads.
issues.detail: When nextDescriptor is nil at this level, the loop body below this builder will not produce a valid rateLimit (the function returns the parent's limit or nil). The carefully-built valueToMetricFullKey for the unmatched entry is never observed. Either short-circuit out of the builder loop when nextDescriptor is nil, or document explicitly that the appended segment is discarded.

issues.description: Naming: matchedUsingValue is true also when matchedViaWildcard is true, but the two branches are written as if mutually exclusive.
issues.detail: matchedUsingValue is initialized to (nextDescriptor != nil) before the wildcard branch sets matchedViaWildcard, so a wildcard match sets both flags true. The if/else if/else chain works only because matchedViaWildcard is checked first. The reader has to derive this from execution order rather than from the variable names. Rename to clarify (e.g., matchedExplicitKeyValue) or restructure as a small enum.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The feature is plausibly correct on the provided tests, but the implementation rests on an unstated invariant repeated across three branches and a load-bearing cross-function assumption about FullKey. There is a clear dead allocation in the override path (NewRateLimit's stats are immediately overwritten), and the new builder runs on every GetLimit call with no benchmark — premature work on the hot path. Consolidate the three branches into one stated invariant, guard the builder behind an ancestor-flag check, and remove the wasted NewRateLimit call before merge.
